concepts.def: Policies raising potential GDP by improving the quantity or quality of factors of production.
Tax cuts, deregulation, privatisation, weakening unions; Friedman (1962) Capitalism and Freedom programme.
Education, infrastructure, R&D subsidies; aim to overcome market failures in human and physical capital.
Laffer (1974): tax revenue rises then falls with tax rate; cuts may raise revenue beyond turning point.
UK output per hour stagnant since 2008 financial crisis despite rising employment (ONS 2023).
Solow (1956): long-run growth depends on technological progress; capital accumulation has diminishing returns.
